races.name: Irish EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Paphos
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown running style, Declan Carroll's runner carries the unknown-quantity flag and could hold untapped ability; going poses no concern but the tactical profile is genuinely opaque and the trainer's recent 14-day strike rate (0/12) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Star
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners this hold-up type for Michael & David Easterby, who have been active lately, but a sole run of 11th from 6f on good is the only evidence base and a tendency to fade late is a concern around this sharp 5f track.

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides this consistent front-runner who has placed in both career starts over 6f and 5f on good ground, making him the most exposed and reliable pace-setter in the field; the key question is whether a prolonged duel with Sable Noir blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: By Jove Grace
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's runner showed a placed effort last time from 5f on good ground and has a healthy trainer strike rate, but this horse's natural hold-up style is compromised here — the crowded pace map means it cannot get to the rear it wants, effectively racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope combine with a prominent-racing type who has accumulated six runs on good ground over 5f with honest consistency; the placed record is modest but the style is perfectly suited to a race where two leaders may exhaust each other.

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up runner has only a fifth-place debut over 5f on good to reference, and with 90 runners under the trainer in 14 days at 3/90, a sharp improvement needs to come from somewhere not yet visible in the form.

runners_data.name: La Flor Granada
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners this lightly raced Fahey runner, whose sole start came over 6f on soft ground — the step up to good going and drop to 5f are both unknowns, and a noted tendency to fade in the finish is a material worry at a track that rewards horses who hold their gallop.

runners_data.name: Sable Noir
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides Kevin Ryan's front-runner who finished eighth on debut over 5f on good ground 63 days ago; the 9-week gap is the longest in the field, and a noted tendency to fade raises a genuine flag if it gets into a duel with The Mean Fiddler from the first stride.

races.paceDynamic: Sable Noir and The Mean Fiddler are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely pressured gallop over this sharp 5f at Musselburgh on good ground. With two horses competing for the same space at the front, neither is likely to get a completely uncontested lead, meaning the pace will be honest-to-brisk rather than artificial or dawdling. Calef will track prominently just off the pace, while By Jove Grace — a true hold-up type — has been mapped to midfield because the field contains more rear-runners than the race shape can accommodate at the back. This contested pace dynamic, with no single horse able to fully control the tempo, marginally favours horses who can travel prominently just off the duel and produce a sustained finish — the prominent-to-midfield profile is best placed to exploit any leaders who tie each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sable Noir and The Mean Fiddler fight for the lead and set a strong gallop, a prominent tracker delivers the winning run
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through the early stages of this 5f, and a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace inherits the advantage in the final furlong on good ground at Musselburgh

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes dominance early and the other drops off, the leader settles into a controlled rhythm and dictates
scenarios.body: A lead horse — most likely The Mean Fiddler given its consistent placed record over course-relevant trips — sets a metronomic pace and proves hard to peg back; horses tracking wide or deep are left with too much to do

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce from the break and the field spreads wide, fresh legs from the rear make late ground
scenarios.body: A true hold-up runner benefits from the leaders hitting a wall in the final 100 yards; however, this outcome is discounted because By Jove Grace — the most likely beneficiary — is racing out of natural role having been pushed into midfield by the congested pace map

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Gallop, Sprinter Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the pace proves deceptively steady, a horse with a sharp turn of foot wins a sprint for home
scenarios.body: A moderate tempo compresses the field and turns the race into a dash from two furlongs out; a horse with natural speed reserves — particularly one yet to reveal full ability — bursts clear

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sable Noir or The Mean Fiddler gains the early upper hand — if neither concedes, the pace duel could compromise both their finishing efforts and hand the race to a prominent tracker like Calef.

Sable Noir's 63-day absence combined with a fading profile in its only start makes it a horse to monitor carefully in the final furlong — a bold show early could turn into a weakening run under pressure.

By Jove Grace is a genuine hold-up type who cannot get to its preferred rear position in this race shape; watch whether Oisin Orr attempts to drop it in anyway or pushes forward into an uncomfortable role.
La Flor Granada's sole form comes on soft ground over 6f — this is a significant class and going shift; watch how it travels in the early stages for clues about whether the conditions suit.
Paphos is entirely unexposed with an unknown running style — watch its early positioning from the gates as that will reveal whether it factors into any of the pace scenarios.

races.name: National Racehorse Week Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's yard is in fine form (5 wins from 21 in 14 days) and this filly steps up to a mile on Good ground having placed twice at 6f on Good; wears headgear and was last seen just 7 days ago, suggesting fitness is sharp — a prominent pitch suits her well and the step in trip looks logical.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner whose entire form book reads over 7f-8f on Good ground, giving him the strongest trip and going profile in the field; placed at 3/7f on Good, he is a genuine hold-up horse who should secure his natural position at the rear and has the stamina credentials to finish powerfully if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly has form at 7f-8f on Good ground and is a confirmed hold-up type, but with three other closers in the field she is unlikely to get the clean passage that style demands; her OR of 52 and record of 0 wins, 0 places from five starts limits confidence even if things fall right.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Etoile
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's two-year-old is the lone pace-setter in the race and Andrew Mullen can control fractions completely from the front; however, his form reads nine, five, twelve, seven from four starts including two on Good ground without a placing, so his role here is tactical rather than competitive at the business end.

runners_data.name: Astral Calling
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's runner has form reads of 12, 7, 6 — all on Good or Standard — and is a natural hold-up horse whose style is compromised by the crowded rear section; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, he is likely racing out of his ideal position and his modest OR of 49 offers little compensating class edge.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners this filly who has winning form at 7f on Good ground (one win from nine turf runs on similar going) and placed form in the top three; a hold-up runner by style but with the strongest win credentials among the closers, her in-form trainer Phillip Makin (1/6 in 14 days) is worth noting and she is equipped with blinkers.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Rocket
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's colt has run three times, all on Good or Standard ground at 6f-7f, with form figures of 8, 7, 5 suggesting modest ability; a true hold-up runner who is compressed into a contested midfield in this shape, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 and no form figures to inspire, the race is likely to pass him by.

races.paceDynamic: Le Grand Etoile is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the gates, Andrew Mullen can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Musselburgh's flat mile without being harassed. Forest Berry will slot in directly behind from a prominent pitch, with Rule Of The Agency and Bluestone Lady tracking at varying distances in the early stages. The bulk of the remainder — The Resdev Rocket, Bonjour Belle, and Astral Calling — are true hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; none of them are likely to secure their natural position, and that compromise diminishes their winning prospects materially. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-handy profile: with a solo, uncontested pace-setter and a flat track, horses who travel close to the tempo without burning fuel will be best placed when the sprint for home begins, and genuine closers face the double handicap of a moderate pace and having to find a wide passage from a contested midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lead Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Le Grand Etoile sets a sustainable gallop unchallenged and Forest Berry or Bluestone Lady track within two lengths turning in.
scenarios.body: Le Grand Etoile controls fractions on Good ground, and horses who have been travelling sweetly in the first two slots inherit a decisive momentum advantage at the two-furlong pole; Musselburgh's flat home straight offers no natural trigger for late closers to accelerate past.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Le Grand Etoile pushes on early and the pace proves stronger than expected, leaving hold-up types with genuine ground to make up.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated first half-mile could flatten out the pace-setter inside the final furlong, creating a brief window for a relentless stayer to reel in the leaders; Rule Of The Agency, who has run over 8f on Good ground, is best placed among the deeper-lying horses to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Bursts Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final quarter-mile and a gap opens down the inside or wide on the home turn.
scenarios.body: A genuine late-finishing scenario requires a pace breakdown that is unlikely with only one front-runner setting a measured tempo; Bluestone Lady, who has winning form on Good ground at 7f and holds a higher ceiling than the other hold-up types, is the most credible beneficiary if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a slow pace bunches the field, causing a wide-open sprint finish with positional chaos across the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A compressed field at this distance on Good ground can produce an unpredictable sprint that scrambles form, but this outcome depends on Le Grand Etoile going conspicuously steady — against his running style — and is the least supported scenario; Forest Berry's sharp finishing speed in this scenario remains the most transferable asset.

watchPoints.text: Forest Berry and Bluestone Lady are both drawn to track Le Grand Etoile closely — watch which horse settles better in the first three furlongs, as the one who travels more easily will be first to strike turning for home.

Le Grand Etoile has not placed in four career starts and if he fades sharply inside the final two furlongs the race could split wide open for horses at opposite ends of the pace map — monitor his stride at the two-furlong marker.

Rule Of The Agency is the most experienced hold-up horse over this exact trip on Good ground but must navigate a congested midfield at Musselburgh where the straight is unforgiving — a clean run from the home turn is non-negotiable for his chance to fully materialise.

Three horses (The Resdev Rocket, Bonjour Belle, Astral Calling) are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same ground at the rear; any interference or traffic among this trio early in the home straight could eliminate multiple runners simultaneously from contention.

races.name: 'Celebrating Veteran Armed Forces' Selling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent form at 10f on good ground (three consecutive top-two finishes), Tim Easterby's 3/90 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's own profile fits this trip and going perfectly; 37 days since last run is worth monitoring for fitness sharpness.|

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with recent race fitness at just 7 days, Tristan Davidson sends this 4yo out in a tongue-tie and he has won and placed multiple times at 8f on good — stepping up to 9f here on a flat track is the key stamina question, but the contested pace role is certain.|

runners_data.name: Theme Park
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with a win and two placings at 8f on good under Faye McManoman, and the tongue-tie is retained; dropping back slightly in handicap company and the sim-going record (13/15 on good) is outstanding for this surface — genuine profile match for this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Despite preferring a hold-up role with six recent runners suggesting a patient style, the overcrowded hold-up market in this field means she'll likely race closer than ideal for trainer Alan Brown; her 0W3P record from 12 similar-going runs and a 12-day turnaround are both fine, but being pushed out of her comfort zone tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4yo has a penholder style that needs things to happen in front of him, and with the field's rear already congested he is likely to find himself racing more prominently than his recent finishing positions suggest is natural; the 0W1P record from 13 similar-going runs and a modest 765654 form string make him hard to trust here.|

runners_data.name: Miners Gamble
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a 3rd at 9f on good which is the standout, but the stable (Brian Ellison, 2/22 14-day) runs two in this race and a going record of just 1 win/place from 15 good-ground runs is a real flag; true hold-up horse who cannot get to the back of this field as it stands.|

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: The 7yo's best placings have come at marathon trips (16f, 17f) suggesting stamina is the weapon, but 1m1f on a flat track may be too short for him to fully deploy that strength; cam Hardie takes the ride and the 75/578 form string shows little consistency, with the overcrowded hold-up berths an additional tactical headache.|

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's 8yo has an excellent sim-going record (13/15, 2W5P) and has won at good ground previously, but recent form at 13f-16f suggests this 9f trip is shorter than ideal — tongue-and-cheek headgear retained, and the mid-division drift in this race could still suit if the pace is truly honest.|

runners_data.name: Titainium
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for Grant Tuer who has run prominently in each recent start, but recent form (57-876) is poor and the step back to 9f on good after moderate efforts at 9f-11f soft/standard is unlikely to spark a revival; Oliver Stammers takes the ride and the contested pace role will be demanding on a horse not in good form.|

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: A genuine course-distance winner (1/9f/GOO) who naturally prefers to be held up, but the field's hold-up congestion means Rhys Elliott (5) will need to push forward earlier than ideal for this 4yo; the 341760 recent string shows inconsistency and the most recent 0 is a concern, though the course form is real.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 6yo has a remarkable consistency record (249222 recent, six placings from his last 13 similar-going starts) and this is his natural trip on his best going; the core concern is that as a genuine hold-up type he will not find the truly clear late run he needs in this traffic-heavy race shape — his upside depends on the pace proving decisive late.|

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Titainium are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gate, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over 1m1f on good ground at Musselburgh. Runninsonofagun has been running over shorter (7f-8f) and will be keen to establish, while Titainium's recent form over 9f-11f suggests stamina is not the issue — the duel between them will set an honest, sustained tempo through the long home straight. With no dominant solo pace-setter able to dictate unchallenged, the race is unlikely to collapse into a sprint finish, meaning the early advantage is eroded and strong-staying types who travel through the race efficiently are best placed. This shape — honest gallop, no extreme pace, flat track — favours prominent racers and efficient mid-division horses who can close into a genuine contest over the final two furlongs, rather than pure hold-up horses who need the pace to truly collapse late. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, with Mayor Of Maghera, Falcon Nine, Princess Niyla, Motawaared, Miners Gamble, and Langton Wold all genuinely preferring to race held up; of those displaced to midfield on the map, Falcon Nine (in-form, multiple placings at this trip on good) and Mayor Of Maghera (course-distance winner) are most likely to actually secure a position closer than their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Titainium fight for supremacy early and set a true honest gallop that stretches the field, setting up a staying finish for horses travelling efficiently through the race.
scenarios.body: The duel up front will burn both pace-setters out before the home straight, leaving the race to horses who have settled mid-division and can sustain their effort over Musselburgh's flat run-in. Yermanthere, Theme Park and Simple Star — all genuine hold-up/mid-division types with good going records — are best suited to grind past a tiring front pair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair, One Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Runninsonofagun or Titainium seizes a clear lead and the other fades early, allowing a solo front-runner to control the tempo and dictate.
scenarios.body: A solo leader from the front at a controlled gallop gives the remaining field a false target to aim at, and Musselburgh's flat straight doesn't always play to closers if the leader conserves enough energy. Runninsonofagun, who won at 8f on good ground and has recent race fitness (7 days), is more likely to sustain it if Titainium concedes the lead after the early duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Improver Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between the two leaders is brisk enough to set up a strong late run from a horse tracking in third or fourth and never over-committing.
scenarios.body: Horses like Theme Park (3 consecutive places at 8f on good, recent winner) and Yermanthere (who won at 10f on good twice in recent history and is suited by this trip) have the tactical profile to sit just off the pace and arrive with a challenge when the pace-setters crack. The flat track and good ground rewards sustained galloping types who find a rhythm early rather than those forced wide or back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Backmarkers Fail to Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly honest and strong, theoretically bringing the genuine hold-up horses into play, but those horses are out of their natural position and unable to reproduce their best form.
scenarios.body: Horses like Falcon Nine, Princess Niyla and Motawaared would need to either be further back than the map allows or push forward out of role, both of which compromise their chance — their redistribution reflects a structural disadvantage in this pace shape. Even Falcon Nine's consistent placed record (six placings, multiple at this trip on good) is tempered by the reality that it will not get the clear, late-run scenario it needs here.

watchPoints.text: Runninsonofagun and Titainium will lock horns from the gate — watch which one concedes the lead first, as the horse that wins that battle controls whether this shapes into a true burn-up or a steadier affair.

Falcon Nine's consistent placed record (249222) at this trip on good ground makes it a shape-dependent danger — if somehow the pace leads to a late-run opportunity, Oisin Orr will be alert, but watch how far back he ends up in the early stages given the congested hold-up group.

Yermanthere's 37-day absence is notable for an 8yo handicapper — watch how Jake Dickson (5) positions him early; if he's not travelling fluently by halfway his hold-up style may leave him with too much to do.

Theme Park's tongue-tie, 21-day break and outstanding good-ground record (13/15) make her a key positioning horse to monitor — if Faye McManoman finds a clear path through from midfield turning in, the profile is tailor-made for this race shape.

Langton Wold and Miners Gamble (both Ellison-trained hold-up types) will likely be searching for space at the rear simultaneously — watch for traffic issues down the back straight if the pace is strong and the field fans out.

races.name: Ina And Ella MacGregor Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Viper
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Brian Ellison with recent Musselburgh-type form; won over 7f on Standard and has placed twice at the trip, making this distance his optimum, and his ability to dictate is the key variable in the race shape.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Scholar
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride for the Easterbys; 73 days off but boasts a solid 1W4P record in similar Good conditions and has placed three times at 7f Good, making him the most credible hold-up finisher if the pace genuinely tests the front-runners.

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partnerships with Edward Bethell have been in solid nick (T14: 7/30); steps up from 6f where he placed twice on Good ground, and 3/4 runs in similar conditions suggest the trip and surface are no concern — a genuine prominent racer who should travel comfortably just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan returns to ride this Tim Easterby 3yo, who owns a win over 7f Good and comes in fresh off a 12-day turnaround; trainer strike rate is modest at T14: 3/90 and the distance profile skews long (most recent runs at 8f), so this may represent a trip relief angle.

runners_data.name: Yy Spirit
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's lightly-raced filly has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; her natural inclination is to race from the rear but with several genuine hold-up types in this field, she is unlikely to secure that position, and the style compromise substantially reduces her prospects in a shape that already bypasses late finishers.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 3yo is the second confirmed front-runner and was placed in 3 of 7 Good/similar-going runs; she will contest the early lead with Viper but, at OR=62, is the lower-rated of the two pace-setters and may find the sustained pressure of a dual-lead contest costly in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is striking at 8/43 in the 14-day window and this horse holds five consecutive placed finishes; true running style is off the pace, but with multiple hold-up types in the field it is unlikely to settle as far back as preferred — that positional compromise tempers confidence in its finishing effort despite the consistent form figures.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the mount for Ivan Furtado, whose yard is cold in the 14-day window (T14: 0/15); Blakefell won at 7f Good and has placed at the trip on multiple occasions, giving him a clean distance-and-surface profile — a versatile prominent runner who should get his position without fuss.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's operation is active (T14: 7/41) and Connor Beasley rides this progressive type who has won twice at 7f Good from 11 course-type runs; the strong good-ground form at this exact trip makes him one of the best-qualified horses in the race on a like-for-like basis.

runners_data.name: Siouxpersonic
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's hold-up horse returns after 73 days off with headgear (hood) and a 5/8 record on Good ground; his best form has come at 5-6f and the step to 7f may be stretching his stamina, though the closing profile gives him a live chance if the pace is truly honest.

races.paceDynamic: Viper and Carmel Valley are the two confirmed front-runners in this 10-runner 7f handicap on Good ground at Musselburgh, and with both likely to assert early, a genuinely contested gallop from the outset is the expected shape — neither has the class advantage to simply dominate and ease the tempo. Two Commanders, Blakefell, and Velvet Rhythm will press from prominent positions, meaning the early sections will be honest rather than blistering but sustained enough to stretch the field. This race shape — a competitive, honest pace with multiple horses wanting to race handily — systematically favours prominent-to-midfield types who can travel into the race rather than having to make up ground from off the pace. Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the field contains too many runners wanting the rear positions; of the two true front-runners, Viper holds the stronger recent tactical profile and Carmel Valley, though lower-rated, was running recently and will contest hard for the early lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Viper and Carmel Valley trade honest early fractions, leaving prominent stalkers travelling sweetly into the straight.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop softens the front two before the final two furlongs, allowing a well-placed prominent racer to pick them off with a clean run; Velvet Rhythm and Two Commanders, with strong good-ground form over 7f, are ideally positioned to capitalise on their consistent proximity to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Viper breaks cleanly and Carmel Valley fails to match strides early, allowing a single pace-setter to control fractions from the front.
scenarios.body: A solo leader over 7f on Good ground at Musselburgh can set a controlled tempo and conserve enough to hold on; Viper's recent Musselburgh-type experience and early speed make this the most credible solo-front scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough between Viper and Carmel Valley that the field strings out and a closing run materialises in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The Resdev Scholar has the most relevant hold-up credentials on genuinely comparable good ground, with a solid 1W4P record in similar going; Siouxpersonic is the other closer with finishing ability, though the redistribution of Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up means any true late surge depends heavily on getting a clear passage through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the dual front-runner duel produces a messy race with checking, bunching, and multiple horses failing to secure their natural positions.
scenarios.body: Disruption through the early and middle stages can leave a horse like Beyond The Bar, who has previously won at 7f Good and is fresh off a 12-day break, finding a gap late from midfield; Blakefell's versatility and 7f course-type experience also positions him to benefit from a chaotic pace shape.

watchPoints.text: Viper and Carmel Valley — watch the first furlong closely; if both break sharply and neither yields, the ensuing duel will set up the race for prominent stalkers and the front pair risk burning out before the final two furlongs.

Velvet Rhythm — Connor Beasley must place him in a ground-saving position early; if he gets squeezed out wide on a tight Musselburgh bend with a busy pack of prominent types, his strong 7f Good profile could be wasted through no fault of his own.

Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up — both are true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the race map; if they drop back to their natural rear position without the pace gap to close into, they are at serious risk of finding the winner long gone before they get organised.

The Resdev Scholar — 73 days off for the Easterbys; Joanna Mason will need to ride him with confidence from the back and his fitness for this first run in over two months is the single biggest variable affecting whether his closing form is reproducible here.

Two Commanders — stepping from 6f to 7f for the first time; his placed form at 6f on Good ground is strong but watch whether he travels with the same fluency once the trip begins to stretch him in the final quarter-mile.

races.name: Ocean Scotland Outdoor Advertising Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer at 5f with one win in last five outings at this trip, wearing tp headgear; natural hold-up type who has been placed on the lead here by redistribution — will need to overcome an unfamiliar role, and the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.80 reflects a meaningful discount if the race demands front-running ability.|

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's consistent mare has placed four times from five starts at this distance and going combination — the class of her recent form is strong; a natural hold-up type but her consistency suggests she can adapt her position, and Paul Mulrennan is well suited to placing a horse from a handy pitch at Musselburgh.|

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: 3yo who showed a placed effort at this trip on Good ground; Billy Garritty rides and the Musselburgh straight suits straightforward profiles, though the horse has been out of the frame more than in it — Good going is fine but wins have not materialised.|

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with four placings from five recent starts, clearly in consistent form and suited by Good ground at 5-6f; a genuine hold-up horse whose instinct is to come late, and while the redistribution into midfield is not his natural position, his recent finishing performances suggest he is in the form of his life.|

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Scored on Good at this trip relatively recently and wears p-headgear; Linda Perratt's eight-year-old is another true hold-up runner pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded rear — his best chance comes if any pace develops, because his 1W4P record in similar going shows he can fire.|

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: 3yo trained by Gemma Tutty whose best recent form includes a close second on Good ground at 5f; Connor Beasley takes the ride and is effective at Musselburgh, though this horse's natural rear-running style is compromised by the field's overall configuration, making a winning run difficult from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith runner wearing t-headgear with a recent win in his last five, but his Going record here (11th, 5th, 6th in recent Good-ground efforts) is modest; Rhys Elliott takes a 5lb claim but the horse's natural hold-up style is squeezed further by the crowded rear of the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Opal Storm is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 5f Musselburgh handicap, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up profile, meaning the early gallop is likely to be measured and uncontested rather than pressured — a sustainable, controlled tempo that rarely produces the gaps needed for true closers to overhaul. The field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types, with So Grateful, Sixcor, Gwen Tennyson, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Lady Bouquet, and Breeze Star all genuine rear-division horses who have been mapped forward simply because there is no space for them all at the back — they will not all find their natural position. With one horse controlling modest fractions over Good ground at Musselburgh's tight, flat 5f, the rail and early position will be at a premium, and the horses best placed to travel prominently from the off — even if that is not their habitual style — hold a clear advantage over those forced to make ground from the rear. The race shape favours runners able to secure a forward pitch inside the first furlong, with those genuine hold-up types likely to find the tempo insufficient to manufacture a winning run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Opal Storm Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Opal Storm leads from the front at a fair pace and no rival has the pace or the position to challenge early.
scenarios.body: Opal Storm, despite being a natural hold-up type, controls this on a soft lead over Good ground at Musselburgh, where a single front-runner at sustainable fractions gives a significant positional edge; Good going suits and the lack of any genuine pace rival means fractions stay within reach of the leader throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If horses able to travel prominently behind Opal Storm track the pace closely and pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Wee Mary and So Grateful, both consistent placers at this distance and going, are best placed to sit just off the leader and produce a sustained challenge; on Good ground Musselburgh's flat finish rewards those who travel in the first three without burning energy early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front-runners tire in the final 100 yards, allowing hold-up types to close.
scenarios.body: Sixcor has form winning off modest pace at this track, and Gwen Tennyson's best run here was a close second when finishing fast; both would need a pace injection that this race shape does not naturally supply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Opal Storm sets too slow a tempo and the entire field converges in the final furlong, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A wall of hold-up horses all arriving together suits the freshest horse or the one widest and clearest of traffic; Lady Bouquet's fresh return after 37 days and Ski Angel's p-headgear could prove small advantages in a chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Opal Storm is a natural hold-up horse placed on the lead by redistribution — watch the opening furlong to see whether the horse accepts the role or idles, because a false pace or a drift off the rail could collapse the entire race shape in seconds.

So Grateful has placed in four of five recent outings and carries strong Good-ground form over this trip — if Joanna Mason manages to steal a position just off the leader rather than accepting the rear, this horse could arrive with a devastating late run that the pace map undervalues.

The cluster of hold-up types — Sixcor, Gwen Tennyson, Ski Angel, Royal Duke — will all be competing for the same ground in the final furlong; watch for traffic problems in the last 2f as up to six horses try to find clear daylight simultaneously off a moderate pace.

Wee Mary has the strongest place record in similar conditions (12 from 15 qualifying runs) and is trained by the in-form Jim Goldie operation (5/35 over 14 days) — if she travels prominently, she is the most consistent performer in the race at this venue and going.
Breeze Star has zero wins or placed efforts on Good ground in recent history — monitor market moves, but the form evidence does not support optimism regardless of how the race is run.

races.paceDynamic: Thats My Boy Luke is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 13-runner mile handicap, though he is a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the lead by default — meaning the pace he sets will likely be measured and sustainable rather than truly aggressive, with no genuine front-runner to push him along or force a contested gallop. With the field overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Due Respect, Approaching Dawn, Joshuas Dream, Caledonian Dream, Abu Royal, Sievier, Misemerald and Bantz all natural closers who cannot all find their preferred position — the early order will be compressed and there will be significant traffic issues in the straight as these horses attempt to find room simultaneously. The clean pace, without genuine pressure, should see the race run at an honest but not extreme tempo on Good ground at Musselburgh's flat mile, which tends to favour horses who travel smoothly through the race and produce one clean sustained effort in the final two furlongs. This race shape most favours the horse who can sit in a handy, prominent position without burning energy early — those who actually manage to race positively from the top will have a distinct tactical edge over the bunched closers who must navigate traffic on a track that does not always reward late, wide runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Thats My Boy Luke sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the field strings out behind without significant early pressure, rewarding those able to travel prominently.
scenarios.body: Thats My Boy Luke dictates at his own tempo and, racing well within himself given the lack of a genuine challenger, stays on stoutly through the final furlong on Good ground; horses that manage to sit just behind the leader in the first three or four positions will benefit from seeing daylight early and avoiding the inevitable backmarker traffic jam.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Surge, Traffic Clears
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just fast enough to stretch the field and those held up wide find a clear run into the straight.
scenarios.body: With a clear passage, the more talented hold-up types — particularly Approaching Dawn and Misemerald, both showing consistent form at this distance on Good — can produce strong late runs, but success depends entirely on drawing a clean line through a congested field.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stalkers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Thats My Boy Luke sets an overly sedate tempo and horses tracking him in third to fifth positions pounce before the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race would compress the field further and turn the contest into a sprint for home, suiting any horse that has tracked close enough to produce an immediate response; Misemerald's strong placed form at 7f-8f on Good and Hostelry's recent winning form make them well placed if they can find a prominent berth.

scenarios.title: Complete Chaos, Wide Draw Wins
scenarios.trigger: If traffic blocks throughout the straight and the winner emerges from an unexpected position after the field fans wide.
scenarios.body: In a 13-runner cavalry charge on a flat track, random positional chaos can elevate any horse that finds an unobstructed path; Elizabeth Bay and Caledonian Dream, though both hold-up types with modest recent records, could benefit from clear daylight if the race falls apart tactically.

watchPoints.text: Approaching Dawn and Misemerald are the two horses with the most reliable recent placed form on Good going at this trip — if either secures a clear passage through the 13-runner field in the straight, they are the obvious dangers to whatever leads.

Thats My Boy Luke is a hold-up horse set to lead by default and may find that role completely foreign — watch for him to be pushed wide or swallowed up if even one other runner is aggressive from the gate, leaving the race without any genuine pace-setter at all.

Joshuas Dream has run exclusively at 5-6f in all five recent starts and is stepping sharply up to 1m here — if the pace is honest rather than slow, watch for this runner to struggle to sustain his effort in the final two furlongs.

Serengeti Sunrise has been off 105 days and shows a repeated finish-fade pattern — monitor in-running to see if she can reverse that tendency, as any sign of travelling well early would be a significant market mover signal.

With 13 runners in a compressed, hold-up dominated field on a flat straight mile, watch the draw and early position at the two-furlong marker — horses fanning widest will have the clearest ground but the most to travel, while those buried on the rail face a lottery.
